rows.title: Canada's payroll employment was little changed in September as manufacturing fell
rows.original_source: Statistics Canada (Survey of Employment, Payrolls and Hours / Job Vacancy and Wage Survey) data
rows.summary: Statistics Canada's payroll survey shows that the number of employees receiving pay rose by only 9,700 (0.1%) in September, after a combined loss of 31,400 jobs in July and August. Health care and social assistance, construction and retail trade added workers, while manufacturing lost 7,300 jobs as US tariffs and high energy costs weigh on factories. Job vacancies rose by 17,300 to 528,100. That is the first monthly increase since December 2025, a sign that some employers are starting to look for workers again. Average weekly earnings reached about $1,358, up 3.3% from a year earlier, though the article warns that this average also moves with changes in hours worked and the mix of jobs. The figures come from a survey of employers, which counts only paid employees and differs from the household-based Labour Force Survey. They arrive just before the Q3 GDP report on Nov. 30 and the Bank of Canada's Dec. 9 rate decision, so they help show how strong the job market really is.
rows.fact: Payroll employment rose by 9,700 (+0.1%) in September, after falling 31,400 in July and August. Manufacturing lost 7,300 jobs, while health care (+7,900), construction (+7,700) and retail (+6,400) gained. Job vacancies climbed 17,300 to 528,100, the first monthly rise since December 2025, and average weekly earnings were up 3.3% year over year.
rows.why: 기업이 고용한 근로자 수와 채용 공고(구인 수)라는 서로 다른 지표가 노동시장의 수요와 공급을 어떻게 보여 주는지, 그리고 관세가 제조업 일자리에 미치는 영향을 이해하는 데 도움이 됩니다.
rows.why_en: It shows how two different measures, paid employees and open job postings, reveal the supply and demand sides of the labour market, and how tariffs can hit manufacturing jobs.
rows.term_def: The number of unemployed people for each open job. A lower number means there are fewer job seekers per open position, so the job market is tighter and finding work is easier.
rows.note: Today's policy item (official data release: Statistics Canada, Payroll employment, earnings and hours, and job vacancies, September 2026). It was released at 8:30 ET on Nov 26, which is 22:30 KST Nov 26, right at the edge of the 24-hour window. It was chosen because Q3 GDP is actually scheduled for Nov 30, not today (confirmed on the StatCan release calendar), and today's Q3 balance of international payments release could not be fetched or verified yet. All key numbers were cross-checked against the StatCan Daily release itself: +9,700 (+0.1%), -31,400 in July and August, +127,800 y/y, vacancies 528,100 (+17,300, +3.4%, first rise since December 2025), weekly earnings $1,357.92 (+3.3% y/y), and an unemployed-to-vacancy ratio of 2.8 (down from 2.9 in August and 3.3 a year earlier). They also match Retail Insider (Mario Toneguzzi, Nov 27) and Wisevoter (Nov 26). The Nov 30 GDP and Dec 9 BoC dates come from the StatCan calendar and a Rio Times brief. Not a repeat: earlier items this week were the budget, Sept retail sales, Macklem's departure and remarks, trade talks, mortgage delinquency and vegetable tariffs, not payroll or vacancy data.

opinion.title: Canada's economy stalls into year-end as hiring freezes take hold: report
opinion.author: Jim Wilson
opinion.summary: This analysis draws on an RBC Economics outlook dated Nov. 20 and a Desjardins note. It argues that Canada's labour market is weak mainly because employers have stopped hiring, not because they are laying people off. The layoff rate held at 0.7%, but only 18.9% of unemployed people found work, compared with a 2017-2019 average of 24.6%. Unemployment rose to 6.7% in October as private-sector employee jobs fell by 53,000. Wages grew only 2.2% a year against 3.1% inflation, so real pay is shrinking, and nearly 30% of Canadians live in households struggling to make ends meet. Desjardins still expects another quarter-point Bank of Canada hike in December, while RBC expects only modest improvement in growth and jobs by year-end.
opinion.why: 해고는 적은데도 실업률이 오를 수 있는 이유(채용 동결)와, 임금 상승률이 물가 상승률보다 낮을 때 가계의 실질 구매력이 어떻게 줄어드는지 생각해 볼 수 있습니다.
opinion.why_en: It explains how unemployment can rise even when few people are laid off, because hiring freezes, and how wages growing slower than inflation shrink households' real purchasing power.

rows.title: US core capital goods orders beat expectations in October
rows.summary: New orders for core capital goods rose 1.2% in October, according to the Commerce Department's report released on Nov. 25. These are non-defense capital goods excluding aircraft, and economists watch them as a proxy for business spending plans on equipment. Economists polled by Reuters had expected a 0.7% gain, and September's increase was revised up to 0.8%. Core orders were 11.2% higher than a year earlier. Reuters ties the strength to the artificial intelligence buildout, which has given business equipment spending three straight quarters of double-digit growth, much of it paid for with heavy borrowing by tech companies. Overall durable goods orders rose only 0.2%, held back by weaker civilian aircraft orders, and the report warns that the boom could lose momentum as investors look harder at AI valuations, funding, profitability and local opposition to data centers.
rows.fact: Core capital goods orders rose 1.2% in October, beating the 0.7% forecast, and core shipments, which feed into the equipment part of GDP, rose 0.6% after 1.3% in September. Total durable goods orders, for goods meant to last three years or more, rose 0.2% after a 2.0% jump in September and were up 8.3% from a year earlier. Transportation equipment orders fell 0.3% because of weaker aircraft orders, while motor vehicle and parts orders rose 0.9%.
rows.outlook: Reuters notes that the strong equipment data could lose momentum as investors grow more skeptical of AI valuations and as worries about AI funding, profits, regulation and data center opposition persist.
rows.why: 기업이 공장 기계나 데이터센터 장비에 돈을 쓰는 '설비투자'가 왜 경제 성장의 핵심 동력이 되는지, 그리고 AI처럼 한 분야에 투자가 몰릴 때 어떤 기회와 위험이 생기는지 이해하는 데 도움이 됩니다.
rows.why_en: It shows why business investment in machines and data center equipment is a key driver of economic growth, and what opportunities and risks arise when investment piles into a single field like AI.
rows.term_def: Orders for long-lasting business equipment such as machinery and computers, leaving out military goods and aircraft because those orders swing wildly from month to month. Economists use it as an early sign of how much businesses plan to invest.
rows.note: 7-day fallback: no major policy/data release in the last 24 hours because Thursday Nov 26 was the Thanksgiving holiday and federal agencies published no major data on Friday morning before this edition. This is the Commerce Department's Census Bureau advance durable goods report for October, released Nov 25 at 8:30 a.m. ET (Nov 25 22:30 KST). Its key numbers were cross-checked against the official Census Bureau release (durgd.pdf): durable goods orders up 0.2% to $346.7 billion, nondefense capital goods excluding aircraft up 1.2% to $89.4 billion, and the September gain of 2.0%. They match the Reuters story. Not a repeat: the items covered earlier were jobless claims, sentiment, the Fed's Cook, Thanksgiving dinner costs, export blacklisting, PCE inflation and the GDP revision, not this durable goods/business investment report.

opinion.title: JPMorgan's chief economist says 2026 was likely 'peak AI'
opinion.author: Samuel O'Brient (reporting views of JPMorgan chief US economist Michael Feroli)
opinion.summary: This piece reports the views Michael Feroli, JPMorgan's chief US economist, set out in the bank's 2027 outlook: AI's boost to overall demand in the US economy will probably peak in 2026. He expects AI capital spending to edge down in 2027, but thinks the drag will be moderate and partly offset by other support, such as falling gasoline prices for consumers. He finds little evidence that AI is causing widespread layoffs, but says the fear that it destroys jobs could weaken workers' bargaining power over pay and lift company profits. He calls AI the dominant feature of the US economy and warns that when growth depends on one engine, any trouble with it matters more. The article also cites Apollo's Torsten Slok, who estimates that AI spending made up 65% of US GDP growth so far this year.
opinion.why: 투자 붐이 영원히 지속될 수 없다는 점, 그리고 경제 성장이 한 산업에 지나치게 의존할 때 그 산업의 둔화가 경제 전체에 어떤 영향을 줄 수 있는지 생각해 볼 수 있습니다.
opinion.why_en: It makes you think about why investment booms cannot last forever, and how a slowdown in one industry can hit the whole economy when growth relies too heavily on it.

rows.title: Korea stands by industrial policy after US tariff proposal
rows.summary: On Nov. 26 Seoul said it is not considering drastic changes to its industrial policies, a day after the US Trade Representative proposed Section 301 'overcapacity' tariffs on Korea and 13 other economies. The US argues that Korean state support for semiconductors, cars and petrochemicals, including the Honam chip cluster plan, cheap loans from state-owned banks and three government megaprojects, helped create global excess capacity and hurt American manufacturing. The proposed combined rate for Korea is up to 15%, the ceiling agreed in last year's deal that tied lower tariffs to a $350 billion Korean investment pledge, but the US kept the option of raising it to 25% if it finds talks or Korea's commitments unsatisfactory. Korea's trade ministry disputed 'substantial parts' of the US report and said the trade balance may have shaped the higher backup rate. The trade surplus with the US reached a record $102.3 billion in the first 10 months of 2026 on AI chip demand, and because exports are about 36% of Korea's GDP, any higher tariff would weigh directly on its growth.
rows.fact: The USTR offered Korea, Japan, the EU and Switzerland 15%, counted after existing duties such as the 12.5% forced-labor tariff from July, with alternative rates of 25% for Korea, 20% for Japan and the EU, and 40% for China. Industry Minister Kim Jung-kwan said keeping the final rate at 15% would be 'more than a success.' The ministry called the claim linking Chinese imports and investment to Korean overcapacity a leap in logic.
rows.outlook: Chang Sang-sik of the Korea International Trade Association's trade institute warned that tariffs could rise further if overcapacity worsens, naming chip tariffs and a possible US probe of Korea's digital rules as key unresolved risks.
rows.why: 정부가 특정 산업을 지원하는 산업정책이 왜 다른 나라와의 무역 분쟁과 관세로 이어질 수 있는지, 그리고 수출 의존도가 높은 한국 경제에 관세가 어떤 위험이 되는지 이해하는 데 도움이 됩니다.
rows.why_en: It shows how a government's support for favored industries can trigger trade disputes and tariffs abroad, and why tariffs are a serious risk for an export-dependent economy like Korea.
rows.term_def: When factories in a country or industry can produce far more than buyers want. The extra goods are often sold abroad at low prices, which can hurt producers in other countries and lead those countries to respond with tariffs.
rows.note: 7-day fallback: no major new Korean policy or data release in the last 24 hours (the Nov. 27 meeting of top financial officials announced no new measures and concerned the already-covered stock stabilization fund). This is the Korean government's Nov. 26 KST response to the USTR's Section 301 overcapacity tariff proposal. The 15% ceiling, the 12.5% forced-labor tariff, the 25% alternative rate, the 13 other economies, the Jan. 5, 2027 comment deadline and the Jan. 25, 2027 hearing were cross-checked against Yonhap reports carried by Korea JoongAng Daily and The Korea Times (Nov. 26) and against Seoul Economic Daily (Nov. 26), and they match. The USTR's fact-sheet page showed no entries when fetched, so the numbers rest on agreement among these outlets. Not a repeat: earlier items this week were producer prices, foreign stock selling, the KOSPI rout and stabilization fund, sentiment surveys and the BOK rate hike, not US trade action.

opinion.title: U.S. Tariff Threat Targets Korea's Chip Projects
opinion.author: Editorial Board
opinion.summary: The editorial says the US overcapacity case names Korea's chip, auto and petrochemical industries and labels the Honam semiconductor cluster government intervention, while holding out a 25% rate as a threat. It admits that politically driven choices about where to put megaprojects, and how large to make them, gave Washington an opening. It argues, however, that using private companies' plant expansions as tariff leverage infringes on Korea's industrial sovereignty, and it rejects the US claims about Chinese trade and weak labor protection. It urges the government to build a 'trade firewall' by stressing the $350 billion US investment plan and Korean factories in America, and to explain its industrial policy better, since companies cannot handle the tariffs alone.
opinion.why: 한 나라의 산업 육성 정책이 다른 나라에게는 불공정 무역으로 보일 수 있다는 점에서, 산업주권과 무역 규칙 사이의 긴장을 양쪽 입장에서 생각해 볼 수 있습니다.
opinion.why_en: It shows that one country's industrial strategy can look like unfair trade to another, and lets you weigh the tension between industrial sovereignty and trade rules from both sides.

rows.title: French preliminary inflation at 3.2% in November
rows.summary: France's statistics agency INSEE said on Nov. 27 that the EU-harmonised inflation rate fell to 3.2% in November from 3.7% in October, well below the 3.6% average forecast in a Reuters poll of 15 analysts. The national consumer price index slowed to 2.9% from 3.4%, also below the expected 3.2%. Energy drove most of the drop: oil product prices fell sharply and outweighed rising gas prices, and services inflation eased as accommodation and transport prices slowed. The background is an energy price shock that pushed euro zone inflation to 4.0% in October, its highest since 2023, after the ECB had already raised its deposit rate to 2.5% in two hikes earlier this year. Spain reported a similar surprise the same morning, with inflation dropping to 4.1% from 4.9%, so the data give the ECB some breathing room ahead of its mid-December meeting, where markets had largely priced in another rate hike.
rows.fact: France's harmonised inflation rate fell to 3.2% in November from 3.7%, and the national CPI fell to 2.9% from 3.4%. Both came in below Reuters poll forecasts of 3.6% and 3.2%. Sharply lower oil product prices were the main cause, along with slower services inflation.
rows.why: 에너지 가격이 물가 전체를 어떻게 끌어올리고 또 끌어내리는지, 그리고 예상보다 낮은 물가 지표가 중앙은행의 금리 인상 판단에 어떤 영향을 주는지 이해하는 데 도움이 됩니다.
rows.why_en: It shows how energy prices can push overall inflation up and then pull it down, and how a lower-than-expected inflation reading can change a central bank's case for raising interest rates.
rows.term_def: An inflation measure that every EU country calculates the same way, so price changes can be compared across countries. The European Central Bank uses it to judge whether euro zone inflation is near its 2% target.
rows.note: Today's policy item (INSEE provisional November CPI, released Nov 27 at 08:45 Paris time = 16:45 KST). The headline CPI (2.9% vs 3.4%) and HICP (3.2% vs 3.7%) were cross-checked against Euronews reporting via Newswav, a separate wire report and XTB's data calendar, and all match. INSEE's own November page could not be fetched (server error). INSEE's October provisional release showed HICP at 3.8%, so the 3.7% October figure Reuters cites appears to be the revised final number. The euro zone October 4.0% figure and the 2.5% ECB deposit rate come from Euronews (Nov 4); Spain's figures come from the companion Reuters report. Not a repeat: earlier items covered UK borrowing and retail sales, the EU budget, euro zone growth, German Ifo, Russia sanctions and the ECB October accounts, not these November inflation flashes.

opinion.title: Economic Calendar: Inflation in Europe surprises to the downside (27.11.2026)
opinion.author: XTB research team (no individual byline)
opinion.summary: This broker commentary sets the French and Spanish November readings against market forecasts. France's CPI came in at 2.9% (consensus 3.2%) and its HICP at 3.2% (consensus 3.6%), while Spain's 4.1% reading against an expected 4.7% was the biggest surprise of the day, with Spanish core inflation easing to 2.6% from 3.1%. The writers argue the softer numbers give the ECB more room to assess price pressures and ease worries about its next decisions. They caution, however, that one softer month is not enough to prove inflation is falling for good. They also note that euro zone consumer confidence improved slightly while services sentiment weakened.
opinion.why: 한 달치 물가 지표만으로 추세를 단정하기 어려운 이유와, 시장 예상치와 실제 수치의 차이가 금리 전망을 어떻게 움직이는지 생각해 볼 수 있습니다.
opinion.why_en: It shows why one month of data cannot confirm a trend, and how the gap between forecasts and actual numbers shifts expectations for interest rates.

rows.title: Core inflation in Tokyo hits 16-month high, bolsters case for BOJ hike
rows.summary: Core consumer prices in Tokyo, which include fuel but exclude fresh food, rose 2.9% in November from a year earlier. That is up from 2.6% in October and the fastest pace since July 2025, though slightly below the 3.0% that markets expected. Part of the jump came from the end of government subsidies for electricity and gas bills, but prices also rose for food, daily necessities and hotel stays, while high energy costs and a weak yen keep pushing up import prices. A narrower measure that also strips out fuel, which the Bank of Japan watches closely, eased to 2.5% from 2.6%, so the rise was driven more by energy than by broad price pressure. Because Tokyo data come out about three weeks before the national figures, they are treated as an early signal before the BOJ's next meeting ends on December 18; the BOJ raised its rate to 1.25% in September after a June hike, and most economists now expect another increase in December.
rows.fact: Tokyo core CPI rose 2.9% year on year in November, up from 2.6% in October and above the BOJ's 2% target for a third straight month. The index excluding both fresh food and fuel slowed to 2.5% from 2.6%. The BOJ's policy rate is 1.25% after hikes in June and September, and it held rates in October.
rows.outlook: Most analysts in a Reuters poll expect a BOJ hike in December and another by end-March, though Sompo Institute Plus economist Masato Koike warned the bank could skip December if market turmoil over AI and chip stocks persists.
rows.why: 보조금 종료나 에너지 가격처럼 일시적인 요인이 물가를 끌어올릴 때 중앙은행이 왜 '근원 물가'를 따로 살펴보는지, 그리고 엔화 약세가 수입 물가를 통해 생활비에 어떻게 전달되는지 이해하는 데 도움이 됩니다.
rows.why_en: It shows why a central bank looks separately at underlying inflation when temporary factors like ending subsidies or energy prices push prices up, and how a weak currency raises living costs through import prices.
rows.term_def: An inflation measure that leaves out both fresh food and energy, whose prices jump around a lot. It helps show whether prices are rising across the economy in general, not just because of one-off shocks.
rows.note: Today's policy item (official data release: Statistics Bureau of Japan preliminary Tokyo ward-area CPI for November, released Nov 27 JST/KST). The Reuters story by Leika Kihara and Takahiko Wada was read in full on WIFC's republication. The 2.9% core and 2.5% core-core figures, the 2.6% October core reading and the 3.0% forecast were cross-checked against Trading Economics' data page and an IndexBox summary of the same Reuters report, and they match. Sources disagreed on the headline Tokyo CPI, so it was left out. The official Statistics Bureau tables sit on e-Stat and could not be read, so the official release itself was not checked directly. Not a repeat: earlier coverage was Japan's national October core CPI, a Reuters poll on the BOJ and BOJ member Tamura's Nov 26 remarks, while this is the new November Tokyo CPI release.

opinion.title: Japanese Yen: Inflation strengthens case for December hike – Commerzbank
opinion.author: Volkmar Baur (Commerzbank strategist); FXStreet Insights Team
opinion.summary: Commerzbank strategist Volkmar Baur argues that November's Tokyo CPI was softer than expected but gives the Bank of Japan little comfort. In his view the downside surprise came from falling fresh food prices, while higher electricity and gas costs pushed inflation up. He says core price growth of about 2.5% shows inflation settling slightly above the 2% target as producer price pressures pass through to consumers, a point hawkish board member Naoki Tamura has also made. Baur expects a hike at the December 18 meeting, with markets pricing roughly an 80% chance, and says the bigger question is how many board members agree with Tamura that rates are still well below neutral. The piece is a short summary written with AI assistance and reviewed by an editor.
opinion.why: 같은 물가 지표를 보고도 전문가들이 일시적 요인과 기조적 흐름을 구분해 금리 전망을 내리는 과정을 보여 주며, '중립 금리'라는 개념이 중앙은행의 금리 인상 속도 논쟁에 어떻게 쓰이는지 알 수 있습니다.
opinion.why_en: It shows how analysts separate one-off factors from the underlying trend in the same inflation data to forecast rates, and how the idea of a 'neutral' rate shapes debate over how fast a central bank should hike.
